subject: Private Deployment: Entry Pricing Options & Support Tier Tradeoffs
messages:

Subject: Evaluating private deploy options — budget & amortization questions

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Soteria is excited about the latency and data control benefits of Redwood Private. I’m starting the procurement conversation and I need two quick things to align with our finance and infra teams: 1) can you outline alternative commercial constructs for a VPC/on-prem deployment (esp. platform fee amortization vs. credits), and 2) are there support tier swaps that would allow us to reduce the up-front platform fee in exchange for a higher SRE retainer?

We have a ~36 month runway for procurement approval and would prefer a model that minimizes capex in Q3. I’m attaching a short tech profile and our procurement intake form. Our procurement lead (cc’d on follow-ups) is Daniel Park.

Attachments: Soteria_Tech_Profile.pdf (doc stub), Procurement-Intake-Form.docx (doc stub)

Thanks,
Emma Larson

Soteria Health
emma.larson@soteriahealth.com
From: markus.klein@redwoodinference.com (Markus Klein)

Cc: monica_patel@redwoodinference.com, neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, May 8, 2025 at 12:45 PM -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluating private deploy options — budget & amortization questions

Emma — great to hear, and thanks for the docs. High-level we typically present three commercial entry patterns for Private (VPC/on-prem):

1) Prepaid capacity credits + low platform fee: customer prepays an annualized token/node credit pool; platform fee is minimal (start-up onboarding only). Pros: predictable unit economics, lower initial platform fee. Cons: higher up-front cash.

2) Amortized platform fee (36-month schedule) + moderate support retainer: spread the platform fee across the contract term as a line item with quarterly invoices; support tiers can be adjusted (Standard -> Premium) to move some cost from platform fee to ongoing retainer. Pros: friendly to capex constraints, simpler procurement. Cons: slightly higher total cost over time vs. prepaid.

3) Consumption-first (no platform fee) + elevated SRE retainer and implementation milestone payments: removes platform fee but increases monthly SRE/retainer line. Pros: minimal capex, aligned with consumption. Cons: operational risk; higher OPEX for sustained usage.

Proposed quick asks so I can put numbers together:
- Target committed monthly tokens or a node-equivalent baseline (ballpark is fine)
- Preference between minimizing upfront fee vs minimizing cumulative cost
- Any mandatory procurement constraints (PO net terms, capital vs expense treatment)

I’ve attached a simple pricing matrix with illustrative numbers and a draft SOW (Soteria_MA_Pricing_Table.xlsx, SOW-draft-v2.pdf). If you’re open, Monica (CS) can run a short MQL to map expected throughput so we model amortization properly. Neha (Finance) is cc’d — she’ll flag anything that needs legal/finance-level approvals.

Attachments: Soteria_MA_Pricing_Table.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), SOW-draft-v2.pdf (pdf stub)

— Markus

Thanks Markus — this is really helpful. A few clarifications from our side: we expect baseline steady-state throughput equivalent to ~4 A100-class nodes, with burst to 8 during peak inference windows. Our procurement preference is option 2 (amortized platform fee over 36 months) because capital committees prefer predictable charges in operating budgets.

Two asks before we lock: 1) can you show a 36-month amortization with quarterly invoices and the impact on monthly runrate if we pick Standard vs. Premium support (Premium includes 24/7 SRE retainer + one on-call engineer during migration), and 2) can we get a migration retainer credit if we commit to a 36-month term (e.g., waive first-month platform fee or provide implementation credit)?

Daniel (procurement) — we’ll need PO terms: Do you accept Net 45? We can push for Net 30 if necessary.

Emma
From: markus.klein@redwoodinference.com (Markus Klein)
To: Emma Larson <emma.larson@soteriahealth.com>

Date: Mon, May 12, 2025 at 4:45 PM -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluating private deploy options — budget & amortization questions

Emma / Daniel — appreciate the clarity. Quick responses and next steps below.

1) Amortization model: we can present a 36-month amortization with quarterly billing. Attached is a short example showing three scenarios (Standard support, Premium support, Premium+Migration-credit). For your baseline (4 node steady, burst to 8) the monthly run-rate delta between Standard and Premium is ~12%. I’ll convert to exact $ numbers once you confirm expected sustained RPS and token distribution for peak windows.

2) Migration retainer credit: yes — for a 36-month committed term we can offer either (A) waiver of the first-month platform fee or (B) a $75k implementation credit applied across the first three quarters. Option B is our preference as it smooths revenue recognition and gives SRE runway.

3) Net terms: Neha — can you confirm if Net 45 is acceptable for a first-time enterprise deal or if we need to push for PO/PO box prepayment? (cc’d)

Proposed mutual action items:
- Emma/Dev team: provide sample token distribution and a short throughput file (1–2 days) so we model peak vs baseline.
- Daniel: confirm procurement terms (Net 30 vs Net 45) and any internal approval windows.
- Markus/Monica: produce a formal commercial term sheet with the three alternatives and numerical amortization for your review by Wed 5/14.

Link: HubSpot deal (DEAL-9876): https://app.hubspot.com/deal/9876

We’ll keep the SOW draft editable and can fold in whichever migration credit option you prefer. Thanks — I’ll have a term sheet in your inbox by EOD Wednesday.

Best,
— Markus
